Comfortable with TypeScript, the React mental model and CSS. No Go, no Vue, and no prior exposure
to Go templates. Knew TypeScript well but not the `!` non-null assertion.

**Why:** explanations that assume Go or Vue syntax is readable land as noise, and the React model
actively misleads in Gitea — HTML is an *input* to the TypeScript (rendered by Go, found via
`querySelector`), not an output of it, and the DOM is the state store rather than any `useState`.

**How to apply:** anchor to TypeScript/React/CSS and say explicitly where the analogy breaks. Note
that Go templates are a substitution syntax closer to Handlebars than to Go the language, and that
most Gitea frontend work needs neither Go nor Vue. See [[teach-through-navigation]].

Verify conventions against the repository before recommending them — survey `git log` for commit
scopes, grep for an attribute or class naming pattern, read the doc that owns the path. State the
evidence alongside the recommendation.

**Why:** the user challenges recommendations ("is this really features worth?") and expects a
defensible answer rather than a confident guess. Several assertions made from memory in this
project turned out wrong: the locale file is JSON not INI, `web_src/css/modules/` is Fomantic
replacements only, and `make lint-editorconfig` exists despite being absent from `make help`.

**How to apply:** when a recommendation is questioned, re-check rather than defend; say plainly when
the evidence overturns the earlier advice. Related: [[teach-through-navigation]].

---
name: local-env-quirks
description: "openSUSE + VS Code setup quirks — Go toolchain mismatch, PATH, clipboard, Prettier conflict"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-09-27T22:13:29.655Z
  originSessionId: a96225c0-b3ad-4c78-bedc-ff767c9a0397
---

- **`make lint-go` stops on `modules/options/options_bindata.go: pattern bindata.dat: no matching
  files found (typecheck)`.** `tools/lint-go-all.go` always lints with `--build-tags=linux,bindata`,
  and `bindata.dat` is a generated, untracked asset. Unrelated to any change; the header step before
  it still runs. Scoped substitute that works: `golangci-lint run --build-tags=linux <pkgs>`.
  (Seen 2026-09-27.)
- **`specstory sync` does not work in this setup** (user, 2026-09-27). Don't remind them to run it
  at wrap-up, despite `AGENTS.md`; they handle AI logs themselves.
- **`make lint-json` fails on `data/indexers/issues.bleve/index_meta.json`** — a runtime file from
  running Gitea locally, in the gitignored `/data`. Not a repo problem; lint the file you changed
  alone: `pnpm exec eslint -c eslint.json.config.ts --max-warnings=0 <file>`. (Seen 2026-09-27.)
- **(Resolved by 2026-09-27: `~/sdk/go1.26.4/bin` is now first on `PATH`.) Local Go was newer than
  the repo's.** `go.mod` pins `go 1.26.4` (CI uses `go-version-file: go.mod`)
  but the system Go is 1.27.0. Two symptoms: `make fmt` silently rewrites `modules/git/key.go`
  (1.27's gofmt re-indents composite literals in multi-value returns), and `make lint-go` *panics*
  rather than reporting findings — `buildir: package "poll" ... unexpected expr: *ast.KeyValueExpr`,
  staticcheck v0.7.0 choking on the 1.27 stdlib. Scoping the lint to one package does not help;
  `internal/poll` is a transitive dep of `net/http`. Fix: `go install golang.org/dl/go1.26.4@latest`,
  `go1.26.4 download`, and put `~/sdk/go1.26.4/bin` first on `PATH`.
- **`~/go/bin` is not on `PATH`.** `tools/lint-go-all.go` does `go install` then execs the bare name,
  so `make lint-go` dies with `exec: "golangci-lint": executable file not found in $PATH`.
- **openSUSE**, so `zypper`. `uv` (needed by `make lint-templates`) is packaged as `python313-uv`,
  though it also `Provides: uv`.
- **The VS Code integrated terminal cannot paste**, images included, so `Ctrl+V` into the prompt
  does not work. Screenshots land in `~/Pictures/Screenshots/`, and reads outside the working
  directory are blocked — `cp` the file into the scratchpad first, then read it from there.
- **Prettier with `editor.formatOnSave` fights the repo's linters** (eslint `@stylistic`, stylelint,
  the JSON check). A gitignored `.vscode/settings.json` disables format-on-save per language, runs
  `eslint --fix` on save instead, and maps `*.tmpl` to HTML for highlighting.

**Why:** each of these cost real time once. The Go mismatch is the worst because it fails as an
unrelated dirty file and a stack trace, neither of which points at the cause.

**How to apply:** if `make lint-go` panics or `make fmt` touches a file you never opened, check
`go version` against `go.mod` before reading the error. Scoped alternatives that work on 1.27:
`golangci-lint fmt <pkg>`, `go vet <pkg>`, `go test <pkg>`. Note `make lint-editorconfig` only
covers `templates .github/workflows options/locale/locale_en-US.json` (`Makefile:144`) — it does not
check `routers/` or new non-Go files. Related: [[prefers-make-targets]].

Use `make <target>` rather than invoking the underlying tool directly — `make lint-js` over
`pnpm exec eslint`, `make test-frontend` over `pnpm exec vitest`.

**Why:** the user asked for this explicitly, "for my own reference" — commands run in a session
double as the list they will run themselves later. A raw `pnpm exec` line teaches them nothing
reusable.

**How to apply:** fall back to the direct tool only when no target covers the case (for example a
single test file: `pnpm exec vitest <filter>`, which `.claude-students/docs/testing.md` documents).
`make help` lists targets, but not all of them — `lint-editorconfig` exists without a help comment.
See [[teach-through-navigation]].
=== /home/mantmant/.claude/projects/-home-mantmant-Documents-CSCI435-gitea/memory/review-dont-fix-student-prs.md
---
name: review-dont-fix-student-prs
description: "On student PRs: report findings, never offer to apply the fixes"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When reviewing a student's PR, hand back the findings and stop. Do not offer to reword the commit,
add the missing trailer, or apply the cleanups — the student makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

**Why:** CSCI435 coursework. Landing several concerns in one commit is the habit being corrected;
a commit that does one thing would have exposed its own missing details at review time. Fixing it
for them removes both lessons. Same principle as [[teach-through-navigation]].

**How to apply:** name each finding with its `file:line` and say which rule or neighbouring code it
conflicts with, so the student can act on it unaided. Verify with the repo's own tooling
(see [[prefers-make-targets]]) and report what passed. End the review at the findings — no "want me
to stage it?".
=== /home/mantmant/.claude/projects/-home-mantmant-Documents-CSCI435-gitea/memory/teach-through-navigation.md
---
name: teach-through-navigation
description: "Wants to learn how to navigate the codebase, not be handed a finished diff"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 818edf5d-cb83-43a8-a993-6bd416b45b01
  modified: 2026-09-12T21:12:57.522Z
---

Explain *where* and *why* before *what*. Name the discovery method — which grep, which doc, which
file answered the question — not just the conclusion. Then give exact edits for the user to type
themselves, and verify afterwards with the repo's own tooling.

**Why:** this is coursework (CSCI435). The deliverable is the skill of navigating an unfamiliar
large codebase; the diff is a by-product. A correct patch handed over teaches nothing.

**How to apply:** start from the user-visible page and work backwards (URL → route → handler →
template → the element). Prefer one generic mechanism over repeated edits across pages, and say why.
Offer to draft prose (docs, PR text) rather than code. Keep it moving — they have said more than
once they do not want to spend hours. See [[evidence-over-assertion]] and
[[prefers-make-targets]].
=== /home/mantmant/.claude/projects/-home-mantmant-Documents-CSCI435-gitea/memory/user-makes-every-commit.md
---
name: user-makes-every-commit
description: "Never run git commit, even with approval; propose small commits and let them commit"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a96225c0-b3ad-4c78-bedc-ff767c9a0397
  modified: 2026-09-27T20:02:09.436Z
---

Never run `git commit` (or amend, stage-and-commit, etc.) on this user's behalf — not even after
they approve the change. Stricter than `AGENTS.md`, which allows a commit once a human approves it.
Plan work as a sequence of small commits, each doing one thing; for each, say which files changed
and why, give a draft Conventional Commit message with the `(#N)` suffix and `Assisted-by` trailer,
and stop so they can review and commit it themselves.

**Why:** stated as a baseline rule on 2026-09-27 ("You CANNOT commit on my behalf, ever"). They
want to understand every change they land, and they don't want time-pressure detours.

The draft message is only a suggestion: they write their own, deliberately brief (upstream squashes
on merge), and said not to review or correct it afterwards (2026-09-27, issue #53).

"Small commits" is for code, where commits guard against breaking changes. Docs-only changes
(`.claude-students/` pages and guides) go in one commit together, not split per doc.

**How to apply:** after each step, stop at "ready for you to commit" with the draft message. Keep
changes careful, catch easy-to-miss details, and flag when `.claude-students` docs need updating
alongside the code. Related: [[teach-through-navigation]], [[review-dont-fix-student-prs]].

Central keyboard-shortcut registry with chords OPEN https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/56
['enhancement', 'scope: medium'] ['ab-wm'] {'number': 3, 'title': 'Sprint 2', 'description': '', 'dueOn': None}
## User Story

As a front-end developer, I want one place to add keyboard shortcuts, including two-key sequences like `g c`, so that I can add a shortcut and have it listed in a help dialog without editing the page-wide key handler each time.

## User Scenario
Nothing changes for the end user in this issue, as all changes attempt to refactor code while keeping the current functionality intact; pressing `s` on a repository home page still focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view focuses the "Go to file" box. Only underlying code will change, where a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` instead of adding another branch to the global `keydown` handler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the repository home page, when the user presses `s` with focus outside a text field, then the code search box is focused and its `S` hint hides; `t` does the same for the "Go to file" box on file and folder views.
- [ ] AC2: Given focus is in a box that shows a shortcut hint, when the user presses Escape, then the box is cleared and loses focus, as it does today.
- [ ] AC3: Given a single-key shortcut such as `?` is added from code, when the user presses that key with focus outside a text field, then its action runs once and the key does nothing else.
- [ ] AC4: Given the two-key sequence `g c` is added, when the user presses `g` and then `c` within 1500 ms, then its action runs once and neither key runs a single-key shortcut of its own.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than 1500 ms, or presses a key that does not finish any sequence, then the `g` is dropped and the second key acts as a fresh press.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in an input, textarea, select or editable area, when the user presses a key that has a shortcut, then no shortcut runs and the key types as normal.
- [ ] AC7: Given a menu or other widget has already used a key (for example a menu jumping to an item when the user types its first letter), when the key reaches the page, then no shortcut runs and any half-finished sequence is dropped.
- [ ] AC8: Given a shortcut already exists for some keys, when code adds the same keys again, or keys where one is the start of the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), then adding it fails with an error; an `S` or `T` hint that loads again, for example while moving through the file tree, is not an error and its key keeps working.
- [ ] AC9: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each one has its keys, a short translated description and, if given, a section label; s and t use their box's placeholder text ("Search code…" and "Go to file") and are in the repository section.

## Out of Scope
- Help dialog that lists the shortcuts, and turning section labels into headings: Issue (#57)
- `g` navigation shortcuts: Issue (#58)
- `c` to focus the comment box: Issue (#59)
- Turning shortcuts off: Issue (#60)
- Shortcuts that use Ctrl, Alt or Cmd (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+K). None of the planned shortcuts need one, so those presses keep being ignored, as they are today.
- Remapping shortcuts by the user, or saving anything to the server.
- The code editor's and Markdown editor's own keys, which stay where they are.

None

As a front-end developer, I want one place to add keyboard shortcuts, including two-key sequences like `g c`, so that I can add a shortcut and have it listed in a help dialog without editing the page-wide key handler each time.

## User Scenario
Nothing changes for the end user in this issue, as all changes attempt to refactor code while keeping the current functionality intact; pressing `s` on a repository home page still focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view focuses the "Go to file" box. Only underlying code will change, where a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` instead of adding another branch to the global `keydown` handler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the repository home page, when the user presses `s` with focus outside a text field, then the code search box is focused and its `S` hint hides; `t` does the same for the "Go to file" box on file and folder views.
- [ ] AC2: Given focus is in a box that shows a shortcut hint, when the user presses Escape, then the box is cleared and loses focus, as it does today.
- [ ] AC3: Given a single-key shortcut such as `?` is added from code, when the user presses that key with focus outside a text field, then its action runs once and the key does nothing else.
- [ ] AC4: Given the two-key sequence `g c` is added, when the user presses `g` and then `c` within 1500 ms, then its action runs once and neither key runs a single-key shortcut of its own.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than 1500 ms, or presses a key that does not finish any sequence, then the `g` is dropped and the second key acts as a fresh press.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in an input, textarea, select or editable area, when the user presses a key that has a shortcut, then no shortcut runs and the key types as normal.
- [ ] AC7: Given a menu or other widget has already used a key (for example a menu jumping to an item when the user types its first letter), when the key reaches the page, then no shortcut runs and any half-finished sequence is dropped.
- [ ] AC8: Given a shortcut already exists for some keys, when code adds the same keys again, or keys where one is the start of the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), then adding it fails with an error; an `S` or `T` hint that loads again, for example while moving through the file tree, is not an error and its key keeps working.
- [ ] AC9: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each one has its keys, a short translated description and, if given, a section label; s and t use their box's placeholder text ("Search code…" and "Go to file") and are in the repository section.

- `c` to focus the comment box: Issue (#59)
- Turning shortcuts off: Issue (#60)

## User Story
As a Gitea user who navigates by keyboard, I want shortcuts to be declared in one place with
support for key sequences and modifiers, so that new shortcuts can be added consistently and
listed in one dialog instead of being hard-coded one at a time.

## User Scenario
Nothing visible changes for an end user in this issue: pressing `s` on a repository home page
still focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view still opens the file finder. What
changes is underneath — a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` with the
keys, a category and a description, instead of adding another branch to the global `keydown`
handler. The next two issues (the help dialog and the `g` chords) read that registry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the repo home page, when the user presses `s` outside an input, then the sidebar
      search input receives focus and the `<kbd>S</kbd>` hint hides — i.e. the behaviour in
      `templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl` is unchanged after the refactor.
- [ ] AC2: Given a shortcut registered as a two-key sequence `g c`, when the user presses `g` then
      `c` within the chord timeout, then its handler runs exactly once and neither key reaches its
      own single-key handler.
- [ ] AC3: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than the chord
      timeout before pressing `c`, then the sequence is abandoned and `c`'s own single-key
      shortcut runs instead.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is inside an `input`, `textarea`, `select` or a `contenteditable` element,
      when any registered character shortcut key is pressed, then no shortcut handler runs and the
      keystroke is not prevented.
- [ ] AC5: Given a shortcut registered with a modifier (for example `mod+k`), when the user
      presses it, then the handler runs — the current unconditional bail-out on
      `ctrlKey || metaKey || altKey` (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts:35`) no longer blocks it.
- [ ] AC6: Given two calls to `registerShortcut` with the same key sequence, when the second one
      runs, then it throws, so a duplicate binding fails at startup rather than silently shadowing.
- [ ] AC7: `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` exists and covers AC2–AC6 with `pnpm exec vitest
      shortcut`, with no browser needed.

## Out of Scope
- Any new user-facing shortcut. `s` and `t` stay the only two bindings after this issue.
- The help dialog (#57) and the ability to turn shortcuts off (#60).
- Remapping shortcuts, or persisting anything to the server.
- The editor-local key handling in `web_src/js/modules/codeeditor/` and
  `web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`; those stay where they are.

## Open Questions
- Chord timeout length. 1500 ms is proposed; GitHub's is roughly a second. Settle it in review.
- Whether `mod` should normalise to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Proposed: yes, one `m

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Keep one document-level `keydown` listener, but move the binding table out of the
DOM and into a JS registry module, and keep the existing `<kbd data-shortcut-keys>` markup working
by having `initShortcutKbd` register a focus handler for each `<kbd>` it initialises.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the DOM as the source of truth and extend the
`querySelector('.global-shortcut-wrapper > kbd[data-shortcut-keys=...]')` lookup on line 57 with
sequence and modifier parsing. (b) Attach per-element listeners via `registerGlobalInitFunc`, one
per shortcut-bearing element, and drop the global listener.

**Rationale:** (a) cannot express a shortcut that has no input to focus — a `g c` navigation chord
or a help dialog has no `<kbd>` sibling to find, and the help dialog in 23.2 needs to enumerate
every shortcut, which a DOM query over hidden and not-yet-rendered elements cannot do. (b) breaks
chords outright, because the first key of a sequence is pressed while focus is on the document,
not on any particular element. A registry keeps one listener, gives 23.2 something to enumerate,
and is unit-testable without a DOM fixture per case.

**Consequences:** Easier — adding a shortcut becomes one call, and shortcuts with no associated
element become possible for the first time. Harder — the registry is module state that must be
populated before the first keypress, so registration has to happen during page init, and a
registry that is not reset between tests will leak bindings across test cases; the module needs an
exported reset used only by tests. It also adds a second place to look when debugging a key, since
the `<kbd>` markup no longer tells the whole story.

## Scope
medium (5 points)

---

---
*Spec drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5) from `docs/sprint1/backlog-refinement.md`, posted by @Jack-Donohue.*
-----
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd);
  if (elem?.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
      return;
    }

    // Don't trigger shortcuts when typing in input fields or contenteditable areas
    if (target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      return;
    }

    // Find kbd element with matching shortcut (case-insensitive), then focus its sibling input
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    // At the moment, only a simple match. In the future, it can be extended to support modifiers and key combinations
    const kbd = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.global-shortcut-wrapper > kbd[data-shortcut-keys="${CSS.escape(key)}"]`);
    if (!kbd) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    elemFromKbd(kbd)!.focus();
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 2

- **Dates:** Oct 13 – Oct 29, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 29, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Oct 22, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 2 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 1 page, and
  every Sprint 0 standard still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 2` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with a `## Tech Debt` section | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint2/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | UML class and sequence diagrams plus Q&A for one medium issue you resolved | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/diagrams/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint2/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 1 issues
  go into the backlog before new work. To skip one, write the reason on that issue (closed, made
  invalid by later changes, or no longer relevant).
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint2/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Tech Debt section (see "Pull request format"). A PR without
  it loses points.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output: summaries,
  screenshots and share links are not logs. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder or
  another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment saying
  so. The site accepts the link in an issue or a PR comment this sprint; the team keeps it in
  **issue comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "UML diagrams (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 150 words on each of: what you have done and what remains; one thing you learned
  about the codebase or about software engineering; one thing you would do differently. Late or
  thin scores 3 of 5.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s1` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), tag after every
  Sprint 2 PR is merged, push the tag to origin, and write release notes listing the features,
  fixes and improvements. The site's example says `v2.17.2`; this fork's base is `v1.27.3`.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## UML diagrams (D6)

The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:

- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`)
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, which embeds both and answers the Q&A

What the diagrams need:

- Show the existing code found during concept location and impact analysis, and the new or changed
  code, and tell the two apart with a legend, colour or label.
- Show only the fields and methods that matter to the issue.
- Annotate the diagrams with the key design decisions and calls. Diagrams without annotations lose
  points.
- Add a short note on how Go maps to UML: structs, interfaces, and embedding.
- The `.md` follows the course template: `# Issue #<N> -- <title>`, `## Class Diagram`,
  `## Sequence Diagram`, `## Q&A`. The Q&A has 3 class-diagram questions, 3 sequence-diagram
  questions and 1 question on AI use, answered "N/A" if no AI was used. Copy the questions from the
  Sprint 2 page.

Grading (15 points): existing code 2, solution code 2, annotations 3, UML notation 2, Q&A 4, AI
transparency 2.

## Sprint report (D8) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, why the team chose these issues, plus a table of title, owner, points,
  scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, next-sprint changes.
- Next sprint plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.
- From Sprint 2: Sprint 1 carryovers (which were taken, which were skipped and why), and D6 and D7
  in the deliverables summary. The report covers this sprint's work only.

##### `?` opens a shortcut help dialog built from the registry []
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user who suspects Gitea has keyboard shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on
any page and see every available shortcut grouped by area, so that I can learn them without
reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is looking at an issue. They press `?`. A dialog opens in the centre of the page titled
"Keyboard shortcuts", listing the shortcuts under headings such as "Site-wide" and "Repository",
each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to a description. Focus moves into the dialog;
Tab cycles inside it and does not reach the page behind. They press Escape, the dialog closes, and
focus returns to where it was.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page with focus on the document body, when the user presses `?`, then a
      dialog opens listing one row per shortcut registered in #56, with the keys and the
      description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus
      returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus stays inside
      the dialog and never lands on a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in a comment textarea, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is
      inserted and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a new shortcut is registered with a description and a category, when the dialog
      is opened, then it appears under that category with no change to the dialog's own code.
- [ ] AC6: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog is opened, then the
      title and section headings are rendered from locale keys, not hard-coded English.
- [ ] AC7: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2 and AC4 and passes `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Adding shortcuts. The dialog lists whatever #56's registry holds, which at merge time is `s`,
  `t` and `?` itself.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The opt-out checkbox — that is #60.
- A printable or documentation-page version of the list.

## Open Questions
- Should the dialog also be reachable by mouse, from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue,
  to keep it to one entry point that the e2e test can cover.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element with `showModal()`, not on
Fomantic's mod
##### `g` navigation shortcuts for repository tabs and notifications ['ab-wm']
## User Story

As a Gitea user who knows GitHub's keyboard shortcuts, I want the same two-key `g` shortcuts to perform the same behavior, taking me to a repository's code, issues, pull requests, actions and wiki, and to my notifications, so that I can move around without reaching for the mouse.

## User Scenario
A reviewer is reading a file on a feature branch. They press `g` then `i` and land on the repository's issue list, then `g` then `p` for the pull request list. Pressing `g` then `c` takes them back to the repository's front page on its default branch, the same as on GitHub. From anywhere in Gitea, while signed in, `g` then `n` opens their notifications.

A shortcut only works when its tab is shown. On a repository with the wiki turned off, or one that uses an external wiki, pressing `g` then `w` does nothing at all: no navigation, no error.

| Keys | Goes to | Works when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `g c` | The repository's front page, default branch | The Code tab is shown |
| `g i` | Issues | Gitea's own issue tracker is shown |
| `g p` | Pull requests | The Pull requests tab is shown |
| `g a` | Actions | The Actions tab is shown |
| `g w` | Wiki | Gitea's own wiki is shown |
| `g n` | Notifications | The user is signed in (any page) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a page inside a repository, when the user presses `g` then `i`, `p`, `a` or `w`, then the browser goes to that repository's Issues, Pull requests, Actions or Wiki tab.
- [ ] AC2: Given a page inside a repository while browsing a branch other than the default, when the user presses `g` then `c`, then the browser goes to the repository's front page on its default branch.
- [ ] AC3: Given a tab that is not shown (its unit is disabled, the user cannot read it, or the repository is empty), when the user presses its shortcut, then nothing happens and the page does not navigate.
- [ ] AC4: Given a repository that uses an external issue tracker or an external wiki, when the user presses `g i` or `g w`, then nothing happens and the browser never leaves Gitea.
- [ ] AC5: Given a narrow window where some tabs have moved into the tab bar's "more" menu, when the user presses one of their shortcuts, then it still works.
- [ ] AC6: Given any page while signed in, when the user presses `g` then `n`, then the browser goes to the notifications page; when signed out, nothing happens.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page outside any repository, when the user presses a repository shortcut such as `g i`, then not
##### GitHub's `c` shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the pull request commit picker ['ab-wm']
## User Story

As a Gitea user who knows GitHub's keyboard shortcuts, I want `c` to do what it does on GitHub, starting a new issue or pull request from the list and opening the commit picker on a pull request's changed files, so that I can start new work or narrow a review without reaching for the mouse.

## User Scenario
A maintainer working on a repository's issue list presses `c` and lands on the new issue page, or on the template chooser when the repository has issue templates, exactly as if they had clicked "New Issue". On the pull request list, `c` opens the new pull request page in the same way.

Later, reviewing a pull request's "Files changed" tab, they press `c`. The commit picker opens with its first entry focused; the arrow keys move through the commits and Escape closes it, as they do after clicking it. On an archived repository, where there is nothing to create, `c` on the lists does nothing.

| Page | `c` does | Works when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Issue list | Same as clicking "New Issue" | The "New Issue" button is shown |
| Pull request list | Same as clicking "New Pull Request" | The "New Pull Request" button is shown and enabled |
| A pull request's "Files changed" tab | Opens the commit picker | Always on that tab |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository's issue list, when the user presses `c`, then the browser goes where the "New Issue" button leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser when the repository has issue templates.
- [ ] AC2: Given a repository's pull request list, when the user presses `c`, then the browser goes where the "New Pull Request" button leads.
- [ ] AC3: Given a list whose create button is missing or disabled (for example an archived repository, whose pull request list shows "Compare commits" instead), when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens.
- [ ] AC4: Given a pull request's "Files changed" tab, when the user presses `c`, then the commit picker opens with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as they do after clicking it.
- [ ] AC5: Given any other page, such as an issue's own page or the compare page, when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens.
- [ ] AC6: Given a page where `c` works, when the shortcuts are listed, then `c` is described by the translated label of what it opens ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), and is in the issue section on the lists and the pull request section on the "Files changed" tab.

## Out of Scope
- `r` r
##### Character-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4) []
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56, #57

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts,
so that dictating a word into the page does not fire a shortcut and navigate me away from what I
was writing.

## User Scenario
Someone using voice control finds that saying a word while the page has focus keeps triggering the
file finder. They press `?`, see a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog reading "Enable
character key shortcuts", and clear it. The shortcut list greys out. They close the dialog, dictate
freely, and the setting is still off the next time they open Gitea in that browser.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the shortcut help dialog, when the user clears the "Enable character key
      shortcuts" checkbox, then pressing `s`, `t` or any `g` sequence has no effect.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user reloads the page, then they are still
      disabled.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user presses `?`, then the help dialog still
      opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user re-checks the box, then `s` focuses the
      repo sidebar search again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser with storage blocked, when the page loads, then shortcuts default to
      enabled and no error is thrown.
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3 and AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping individual shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the preference on the server or syncing it across devices or browsers.
- A copy of the toggle in the user settings pages.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 is satisfied by "turn off", "remap" or "active on focus only". This issue
  takes "turn off" as the cheapest complete option; confirm that is the team's reading.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Store the preference in `localStorage` and keep `?` itself exempt from the toggle.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A server-side user setting, as a column on the user table with a
checkbox on the appearance settings page. (b) Storing it in `localStorage` but suppressing every
shortcut including `?`.

**Rationale:** (a) needs a migration and a settings form for a preference that is per-browser by
nature — someone using voice control on one machine does not need it off everywhere

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already spread across many pages, not
for new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** Append `?_ui_performance_trace=1` to the URL to print per-init timings.
`index.ts` already logs an error when total init exceeds 500ms.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- Forgetting the early return in a page-load init means that feature's cost is paid on every page
  in Gitea, which is what the 500ms warning is there to catch.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions
```

import {getCurrentLocale} from '../utils.ts';

/** frontend `Locale.TrN`: pick the `_1` or `_n` form for `count` and interpolate `%d` */
export function trN(count: number, form1: string, formN: string, {lang = getCurrentLocale()}: {lang?: string} = {}): string {
  const form = new Intl.PluralRules(lang).select(count) === 'one' ? form1 : formN;
  return form.replace('%d', String(count));
}

# i18n — locale files and translation

**Read when:** adding or changing any user-visible string.
**Not here:** using a key in a template -> `templates.md`; in TypeScript -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

The translated strings and the machinery that looks them up, for both the backend/templates and
the frontend.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | **the only file you edit** — the source of truth |
| `options/locale/locale_<lang>.json` | 28 other locales, all generated from Crowdin |
| `modules/translation/translation.go` | locale loading and lookup; requires the `locale_*.json` naming |
| `modules/translation/i18n/` | the lookup implementation and fallback behaviour |
| `crowdin.yml` | the sync config: source is `locale_en-US.json`, translations land as `locale_%locale%.json` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Only ever edit `locale_en-US.json`.** Every other locale file is written by Crowdin
  (`crowdin.yml` sets `en-US` as the source). Editing one by hand is overwritten on the next sync,
  and a PR that touches other locale files will be asked to revert them.
- Keys are dotted and grouped by area (`repo.issues.new`, `settings.`, `admin.`). Put a new key
  next to its neighbours rather than at the end.
- Templates use `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "key"}}`, or `TrN` for plurals. TypeScript uses `trN` from
  `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts`; strings reach the frontend through `window.config.i18n`
  (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl`), which is deliberately limited to general text — anything
  specialised should arrive via an API response, a `data-` attribute, or `pageData`.
- A plural is **two keys** suffixed `_1` and `_n`, both interpolating `%d` — see
  `actions.runs.graph_jobs_count_1` and `_n`. `TrN` and `trN` pick the form from the count.
- The `data-` attribute carrying a string to TypeScript is named `data-locale-<name>`, read with
  `getAttribute` — `templates/repo/actions/view_component.tmpl` passes both plural forms this way.
- **Never write a user-visible literal** in a template, a handler, or a `.ts` file.
- Errors whose message reaches the user go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`
  (`modules-util-and-generics.md`), not a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `crowdin.yml` sets `skip_untranslated_strings` and `export_only_approved`, so a missing
  translation falls back rather than shipping an empty string.

## Recipes

**Add a string.** Add the key to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` in the right group, use it via
`ctx.Locale.Tr` or `trN`, and leave the other locale files alone.

**Add a plural.** Two keys named `<key>_1` and `<key>_n` plus `TrN` / `trN`; the count argument
selects the form.

**Add a string the frontend needs.** Prefer a `data-locale-<name>` attribute or `pageData` from the
handler. Only genuinely general text belongs in the global `window.config.i18n` object.

## Gotchas

- A missing key renders as the key itself — visible in the UI but easy to miss on a rarely-hit
  branch.
- Changing an existing key's *text* is fine; changing the *key name* invalidates every existing
  translation for it.
- Only a `bindata` build embeds `options/locale` (`modules/options/options_bindata.go`) and needs a
  rebuild for a locale change. A plain build reads the files from disk at startup
  (`modules/options/options_dynamic.go`), and outside `RUN_MODE = prod` reloads them on change
  (`modules/translation/translation.go` → `WatchLocalChanges`).
- Some keys are built from an enum's name while rendering: `actions.status.%s`
  (`templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl`), and five families under `repo.issues.` for a close
  reason: `close_reason.%s` and `close_as.%s` (`repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`, `filter_actions.tmpl`),
  `close_as_with_comment.%s` (`view_content.tmpl`), `closed_as.%s` (`view_content/comments.tmpl`)
  and `closed_title_as.%s` (`shared/close_reason_icon.tmpl`). Grepping the full key finds no use, so
  grep the prefix before deleting a key that looks unused, and give a new enum value a key in every
  family that builds from it.

## Related

- `templates.md` — `ctx.Locale.Tr` and where strings are used
- `frontend-js.md` — the TypeScript side
```

import type {Promisable} from '../types.ts';

let globalSelectorObserverInited = false;

type SelectorHandler<T extends Element> = {selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void};
const selectorHandlers: SelectorHandler<Element>[] = [];

type GlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event> = (el: T, e: E) => Promisable<void>;
const globalEventFuncs: Record<string, GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>> = {};

type GlobalInitFunc<T extends Element> = (el: T) => Promisable<void>;
const globalInitFuncs: Record<string, GlobalInitFunc<Element>> = {};

// It handles the global events for all `<div data-global-click="onSomeElemClick"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event>(event: string, name: string, func: GlobalEventFunc<T, E>) {
  globalEventFuncs[`${event}:${name}`] = func as GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>;
}

// It handles the global init functions by a selector, for example:
// > registerGlobalSelectorObserver('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => { initDropdown(el, ...) });
// ATTENTION: For most cases, it's recommended to use registerGlobalInitFunc instead,
// Because this selector-based approach is less efficient and less maintainable.
// But if there are already a lot of elements on many pages, this selector-based approach is more convenient for exiting code.
export function registerGlobalSelectorFunc<T extends Element>(selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void) {
  selectorHandlers.push({selector, handler: handler as (el: Element) => void});
  // Then initAddedElementObserver will call this handler for all existing elements after all handlers are added.
  // This approach makes the init stage only need to do one "querySelectorAll".
  if (!globalSelectorObserverInited) return;
  for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<T>(selector)) {
    handler(el);
  }
}

// It handles the global init functions for all `<div data-global-int="initSomeElem"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalInitFunc<T extends HTMLElement>(name: string, handler: GlobalInitFunc<T>) {
  globalInitFuncs[name] = handler as GlobalInitFunc<Element>;
  // The "global init" functions are managed internally and called by callGlobalInitFunc
  // They must be ready before initGlobalSelectorObserver is called.
  if (globalSelectorObserverInited) throw new Error('registerGlobalInitFunc() must be called before initGlobalSelectorObserver()');
}

function callGlobalInitFunc(el: Element) {
  // TODO: GLOBAL-INIT-MULTIPLE-FUNCTIONS: maybe in the future we need to extend it to support multiple functions, for example: `data-global-init="func1 func2 func3"`
  const initFunc = el.getAttribute('data-global-init')!;
  const func = globalInitFuncs[initFunc];
  if (!func) throw new Error(`Global init function "${initFunc}" not found`);

  // when an element node is removed and added again, it should not be re-initialized again.
  type GiteaGlobalInitElement = Partial<Element> & {_giteaGlobalInited: boolean};
  if ((el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited) return;
  (el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited = true;

  func(el);
}

    const func = globalEventFuncs[`click:${funcName}`];
    if (!func) throw new Error(`Global event function "click:${funcName}" not found`);
    func(elem, e);
  });
}

I've read through it. Here's where things stand before we change anything.

**What's there now** (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`, the only file involved)
- There's one `keydown` listener for the whole document. When a key is pressed, it searches the DOM for `.global-shortcut-wrapper > kbd[data-shortcut-keys="<key>"]` and focuses the input next to it. The HTML is the only record of which shortcuts exist, so the code can't list them, can't handle a two-key sequence, and can't run a shortcut that has no input.
- The hints live in three places: `templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl` (`s`), `RepoFileSearch.vue` (`t`) and `templates/devtest/keyboard-shortcut.tmpl`.
- When you move through the file tree, `ViewFileTreeStore.ts` replaces the `.repo-view-content` HTML. The old `<kbd>` elements leave the page and new ones get set up. That's the "hint that loads again" case in AC8.
- AC7 is easy to detect: `aria-menu.ts:147-152` calls `preventDefault()` when the user types a letter to jump in a menu, so the page sees `e.defaultPrevented`.
- AC9's section label can reuse the existing locale key `repository` ("Repository"), so no new string is needed. The descriptions are the input placeholders, which the server has already translated.
- There are no tests for shortcuts yet (unit or e2e). Vitest runs on happy-dom, so all of this can be unit-tested.

**Three course-process gaps to know about**
1. The issue body says "Design Decisions: Below", but nothing follows. D3 is graded strictly. I'll log decisions in `.specstory/issue-56-design-decisions.md` as we make them.
2. There's no `Spec reviewed — …` comment from a teammate yet. D2 says that comes before coding.
3. Branch names must start with `feat/`, `fix/` or `chore/` (`STUDENTS.md:216`). `refactor/` isn't on the list. The branch is local only, so `git branch -m feat/issue-56-shortcut-registry` fixes it.

**Proposed commits**, each with its tests:
1. The registry and how it handles keys (sequences, the 1500 ms timeout, conflicts, skipping text fields, keys a widget already used), covering AC3–AC8.
2. Make the `<kbd>` hints register through it and remove the DOM lookup (AC1, AC2, and the reload part of AC8).
3. Descriptions and section labels for listing (AC9).
4. A "how to add a shortcut" recipe in `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` plus its `guide/` twin.

**First decision: the shape of `registerShortcut`.** It matters because #57 consumes it, and so do #58 and #59, which are also assigned to you.

```ts
registerShortcut({
  keys: 'g c',              // a space between keys means a sequence, as the ACs write it
  description: string,      // already translated
  section?: string,         // already translated
  element?: HTMLElement,    // the shortcut only exists while this element is on the page
  action: () => void,
});
getShortcuts(); // {keys, description, section}[] for the current page
```

The `element` field is where the real choice is. If a new registration finds an older one whose element has left the page, it replaces it. A real duplicate still throws. Stale entries also drop out of the list. That fixes the AC8 reload and keeps #57's dialog accurate after file-tree navigation. It also gives #58 ("only when its tab is shown") and #59 ("only when the button is shown") what they need. The alternatives:
- **`registerShortcut` returns an unregister function.** Nothing would ever call it: `data-global-init` has no cleanup step, and the file tree replaces HTML without unmounting the Vue component.
- **The newest registration always wins.** A real clash between two hints would then pass silently, which goes against AC8.
- **Keep looking the element up at key-press time.** That's today's approach. It has no stale entries, but nothing can be listed, and each kind of shortcut would need its own lookup.

Does this API work for you? If so, I'll log it as Decision 1 and start on commit 1.

import {announce, announceSelectionChange} from './aria-announce.ts';

const liveRegions = () => document.querySelectorAll('[role="status"]');

// these tests share document.body and the module's live region, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('announce', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  test('announce-uses-one-region-on-body', () => {
    announce('first');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(100);
    announce('second');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(100);
    expect(liveRegions()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(liveRegions()[0].parentElement).toBe(document.body);
    expect(liveRegions()[0].textContent).toBe('second');
  });

  test('announce-batches-messages-in-the-same-window', () => {
    announce('a deselected');
    announce('b selected');
    expect(liveRegions()[0].textContent).toBe('');

    expect(Array.from(liveRegions()[0].children, (el) => el.textContent)).toEqual(['a deselected', 'b selected']);
  });

  test('announce-recreates-a-removed-region', () => {
    document.body.replaceChildren();
    announce('again');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(100);
    expect(liveRegions()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(liveRegions()[0].textContent).toBe('again');

    announce('fresh');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(100);
    expect(Array.from(liveRegions()[0].children, (el) => el.textContent)).toEqual(['fresh']);

```markdown
### Decision 1: shortcuts live in a JS registry, and a shortcut can be tied to an element

**Decision:** Add `registerShortcut({keys, description, section?, element?, action})` and
`getShortcuts()` to `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`, served by one document-level `keydown`
listener. A shortcut given an `element` only exists while that element is on the page: a new
registration replaces an older one whose element has gone, and a clash with a live one throws.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- Keep the DOM as the record, as today: on each key press, look for a matching
  `<kbd data-shortcut-keys>`. Lost because a shortcut with no input to focus (`?`, `g c`) has no
  `<kbd>` to find, and nothing could list the shortcuts for the help dialog (#57).
- `registerShortcut` returns an unregister function for the caller to call. Lost because nothing
  would call it: `data-global-init` has no teardown, and moving through the file tree replaces the
  page content without unmounting the Vue file finder (`ViewFileTreeStore.ts`).
- The newest registration of a key always wins. Lost because a real clash between two shortcuts
  would pass silently, which AC8 rules out.

**Rationale:** Tying a shortcut to its element is what lets an `S`/`T` hint that the file tree
reloads register again without an error (AC8), and keeps the list accurate after that navigation
(AC9, #57). It also fits #58 and #59, whose shortcuts only work while their tab or button is shown.

**Consequences:** Adding a shortcut is one call, and shortcuts without an input become possible.
The registry is a class (`ShortcutRegistry`) so tests make their own instance: Vitest here shares
modules between test files (`isolate: false` in `vitest.config.ts`), so one shared registry would
leak between tests. An element that stays on the page but is hidden still counts as present, so
#58 and #59 must tie their shortcuts to an element that is removed, or check visibility in the
action. Debugging a key now means checking the registry as well as the `<kbd>` markup.

```

import {ShortcutRegistry} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('ShortcutRegistry', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  let ctx: ReturnType<typeof setup>;
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    ctx = setup();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  test('AC3 a single key runs its action once and nothing else', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('?');
    expect(press(ctx.button, '?', {shiftKey: true}).defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'x').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC3 keys match regardless of case, and Shift alone is not a press', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('S');
    press(ctx.button, 'Shift', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'S', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 's');
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  test('AC4 a sequence runs once and its keys run no single-key shortcut', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('c');
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'g').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1500);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'c').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(sequence).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(single).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC5 waiting longer than the timeout drops the first key', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('c');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1501);
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(single).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('AC5 a key that finishes no sequence drops the first key and acts as a fresh press', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('x');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    press(ctx.button, 'x');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(single).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'z').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC6 keys typed into a field run no shortcut', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('s');
    for (const field of ctx.root.querySelectorAll('input, textarea, select, [contenteditable]')) {
      expect(press(field, 's').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(action).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC6 typing into a field drops a started sequence', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    press(ctx.root.querySelector('input')!, 'a');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC7 a key a widget already used runs no shortcut and drops a started sequence', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('x');
    ctx.button.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.preventDefault(), {once: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'x');
    expect(single).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    ctx.button.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.preventDefault(), {once: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'b');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('keys pressed with Ctrl, Alt or Cmd run no shortcut', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('s');
    for (const modifier of ['ctrlKey', 'altKey', 'metaKey']) {
      expect(press(ctx.button, 's', {[modifier]: true}).defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(action).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC8 adding the same keys, or keys that start one another, throws', () => {
    ctx.add('s');
    ctx.add('g c');
    expect(() => ctx.add('S')).toThrow('conflicts with "s"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('g')).toThrow('conflicts with "g c"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('g c x')).toThrow('conflicts with "g c"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('c')).not.toThrow();
  });

  test('AC8 a shortcut whose element left the page gives way to a new one', () => {
    const oldElem = document.createElement('kbd');
    const newElem = document.createElement('kbd');
    ctx.root.append(oldElem, newElem);
    const oldAction = ctx.add('t', {element: oldElem});
    expect(() => ctx.add('t', {element: newElem})).toThrow('conflicts with "t"');

    oldElem.remove();
    const newAction = ctx.add('t', {element: newElem});
    press(ctx.button, 't');
    expect(oldAction).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(newAction).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('AC9 listing gives keys, description and section of the shortcuts on the page', () => {
    const elem = document.createElement('kbd');
    ctx.root.append(elem);
    ctx.registry.register({keys: 'g c', description: 'Code', section: 'Repository', action: () => {}});
    ctx.add('t', {element: elem});
    expect(ctx.registry.list()).toEqual([
      {keys: 'g c', description: 'Code', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 't', description: 'run t', section: undefined},
    ]);

    elem.remove();
    expect(ctx.registry.list().map((s) => s.keys)).toEqual(['g c']);
  });
});
