```text
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.toLowerCase();
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}
import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutKbd} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('ShortcutRegistry', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  let ctx: ReturnType<typeof setup>;
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    ctx = setup();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  test('AC3 a single key runs its action once and nothing else', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('?');
    expect(press(ctx.button, '?', {shiftKey: true}).defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'x').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC3 keys match regardless of case, and Shift alone is not a press', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('S');
    press(ctx.button, 'Shift', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'S', {shiftKey: true});
    press(ctx.button, 's');
    expect(action).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  test('AC4 a sequence runs once and its keys run no single-key shortcut', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('c');
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'g').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1500);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'c').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(sequence).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(single).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC5 waiting longer than the timeout drops the first key', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('c');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1501);
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(single).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('AC5 a key that finishes no sequence drops the first key and acts as a fresh press', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('x');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    press(ctx.button, 'x');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(single).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(press(ctx.button, 'z').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC6 keys typed into a field run no shortcut', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('s');
    for (const field of ctx.root.querySelectorAll('input, textarea, select, [contenteditable]')) {
      expect(press(field, 's').defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(action).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC6 typing into a field drops a started sequence', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    press(ctx.root.querySelector('input')!, 'a');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC7 a key a widget already used runs no shortcut and drops a started sequence', () => {
    const sequence = ctx.add('g c');
    const single = ctx.add('x');
    ctx.button.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.preventDefault(), {once: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'x');
    expect(single).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    press(ctx.button, 'g');
    ctx.button.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.preventDefault(), {once: true});
    press(ctx.button, 'b');
    press(ctx.button, 'c');
    expect(sequence).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('keys pressed with Ctrl, Alt or Cmd run no shortcut', () => {
    const action = ctx.add('s');
    for (const modifier of ['ctrlKey', 'altKey', 'metaKey']) {
      expect(press(ctx.button, 's', {[modifier]: true}).defaultPrevented).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(action).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  test('AC8 adding the same keys, or keys that start one another, throws', () => {
    ctx.add('s');
    ctx.add('g c');
    expect(() => ctx.add('S')).toThrow('conflicts with "s"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('g')).toThrow('conflicts with "g c"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('g c x')).toThrow('conflicts with "g c"');
    expect(() => ctx.add('c')).not.toThrow();
  });

  test('AC8 a shortcut whose element left the page gives way to a new one', () => {
    const oldElem = document.createElement('kbd');
    const newElem = document.createElement('kbd');
    ctx.root.append(oldElem, newElem);
    const oldAction = ctx.add('t', {element: oldElem});
    expect(() => ctx.add('t', {element: newElem})).toThrow('conflicts with "t"');

    oldElem.remove();
    const newAction = ctx.add('t', {element: newElem});
    press(ctx.button, 't');
    expect(oldAction).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(newAction).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('AC9 listing gives keys, description and section of the shortcuts on the page', () => {
    const elem = document.createElement('kbd');
    ctx.root.append(elem);
    ctx.registry.register({keys: 'g c', description: 'Code', section: 'Repository', action: () => {}});
    ctx.add('t', {element: elem});
    expect(ctx.registry.list()).toEqual([
      {keys: 'g c', description: 'Code', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 't', description: 'run t', section: undefined},
    ]);

    elem.remove();
    expect(ctx.registry.list().map((s) => s.keys)).toEqual(['g c']);
  });
});

// the markup of templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl and RepoFileSearch.vue
function renderHint(key: string, placeholder: string, section?: string) {
  const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
  wrapper.className = 'ui input global-shortcut-wrapper';
  wrapper.innerHTML = `<input placeholder="${placeholder}"><kbd data-shortcut-keys="${key}">${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`;
  document.body.append(wrapper);
  const input = wrapper.querySelector('input')!;
  const kbd = wrapper.querySelector('kbd')!;
  if (section) kbd.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  initShortcutKbd(kbd);
  return {wrapper, input, kbd};
}

// these tests share document.body and its focus, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('shortcut hints', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    initGlobalShortcut();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    document.body.replaceChildren();
  });

  test('AC1 pressing a hint key focuses its box and hides the hint', () => {
    const search = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    const findFile = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    expect(press(document.body, 's').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(search.input);
    expect(search.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);

    search.input.blur();
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(findFile.input);
    expect(findFile.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('AC2 Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away', () => {
    const {input, kbd} = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    input.focus();
    input.value = 'needle';
    press(input, 'Escape');
    expect(input.value).toBe('');
    expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(input);
    expect(kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC8 a hint that loads again keeps its key working', () => {
    const before = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    before.wrapper.remove(); // as moving through the file tree replaces the page content
    const after = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(after.input);
  });

  test('AC8 a second hint for the same key on the page throws', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    expect(() => renderHint('s', 'Search issues…')).toThrow('conflicts with "s"');
  });

  test('AC9 a hint is listed with its box\'s placeholder and its section', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…', 'Repository');
    renderHint('t', 'Go to file', 'Repository');
    renderHint('x', 'No section');
    expect(getShortcuts()).toEqual([
      {keys: 's', description: 'Search code…', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 't', description: 'Go to file', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 'x', description: 'No section', section: undefined},
    ]);
  });
});

--
## User Story

As a front-end developer, I want one place to add keyboard shortcuts, including two-key sequences like `g c`, so that I can add a shortcut and have it listed in a help dialog without editing the page-wide key handler each time.

## User Scenario
Nothing changes for the end user in this issue, as all changes attempt to refactor code while keeping the current functionality intact; pressing `s` on a repository home page still focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view focuses the "Go to file" box. Only underlying code will change, where a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` instead of adding another branch to the global `keydown` handler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the repository home page, when the user presses `s` with focus outside a text field, then the code search box is focused and its `S` hint hides; `t` does the same for the "Go to file" box on file and folder views.
- [ ] AC2: Given focus is in a box that shows a shortcut hint, when the user presses Escape, then the box is cleared and loses focus, as it does today.
- [ ] AC3: Given a single-key shortcut such as `?` is added from code, when the user presses that key with focus outside a text field, then its action runs once and the key does nothing else.
- [ ] AC4: Given the two-key sequence `g c` is added, when the user presses `g` and then `c` within 1500 ms, then its action runs once and neither key runs a single-key shortcut of its own.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than 1500 ms, or presses a key that does not finish any sequence, then the `g` is dropped and the second key acts as a fresh press.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in an input, textarea, select or editable area, when the user presses a key that has a shortcut, then no shortcut runs and the key types as normal.
- [ ] AC7: Given a menu or other widget has already used a key (for example a menu jumping to an item when the user types its first letter), when the key reaches the page, then no shortcut runs and any half-finished sequence is dropped.
- [ ] AC8: Given a shortcut already exists for some keys, when code adds the same keys again, or keys where one is the start of the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), then adding it fails with an error; an `S` or `T` hint that loads again, for example while moving through the file tree, is not an error and its key keeps working.
- [ ] AC9: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each one has its keys, a short translated description and, if given, a section label; s and t use their box's placeholder text ("Search code…" and "Go to file") and are in the repository section.

## Out of Scope
- Help dialog that lists the shortcuts, and turning section labels into headings: Issue (#57)
- `g` navigation shortcuts: Issue (#58)
- `c` to focus the comment box: Issue (#59)
- Turning shortcuts off: Issue (#60)
- Shortcuts that use Ctrl, Alt or Cmd (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+K). None of the planned shortcuts need one, so those presses keep being ignored, as they are today.
- Remapping shortcuts by the user, or saving anything to the server.
- The code editor's and Markdown editor's own keys, which stay where they are.

## Open Questions
None

+import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutKbd} from './shortcut.ts';

+function setup() {
+  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
+  const root = document.createElement('div');
+  root.innerHTML = `
+    <button type="button">button</button>
+    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
+  `;
+  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
+  document.body.append(root);
+  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
+  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
+    const action = vi.fn();
+    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
+    return action;
+  };
+  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
+}
+
+function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
+  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
+  el.dispatchEvent(e);
+  return e;
+}

import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.toLowerCase();
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // When the matching key is pressed, the sibling input is focused.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Modifier keys are not supported yet
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

import {ShortcutRegistry, getShortcuts, initGlobalShortcut, initShortcutKbd} from './shortcut.ts';

function setup() {
  const registry = new ShortcutRegistry();
  const root = document.createElement('div');
  root.innerHTML = `
    <button type="button">button</button>
    <input><textarea></textarea><select></select><div contenteditable="true"></div>
  `;
  root.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => registry.handleKeyDown(e));
  document.body.append(root);
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  const add = (keys: string, opts: {element?: HTMLElement} = {}) => {
    const action = vi.fn();
    registry.register({keys, description: `run ${keys}`, action, ...opts});
    return action;
  };
  return {registry, root, button, add, cleanup: () => root.remove()};
}

function press(el: Element, key: string, opts: KeyboardEventInit = {}): KeyboardEvent {
  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...opts});
  el.dispatchEvent(e);
  return e;
}

// these tests share document.body and fake timers, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('ShortcutRegistry', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  let ctx: ReturnType<typeof setup>;
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    ctx = setup();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    ctx.cleanup();
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });


// the markup of templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl and RepoFileSearch.vue
function renderHint(key: string, placeholder: string, section?: string) {
  const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
  wrapper.className = 'ui input global-shortcut-wrapper';
  wrapper.innerHTML = `<input placeholder="${placeholder}"><kbd data-shortcut-keys="${key}">${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`;
  document.body.append(wrapper);
  const input = wrapper.querySelector('input')!;
  const kbd = wrapper.querySelector('kbd')!;
  if (section) kbd.setAttribute('data-shortcut-section', section);
  initShortcutKbd(kbd);
  return {wrapper, input, kbd};
}

// these tests share document.body and its focus, so they must not run concurrently (see vitest.config.ts)
describe('shortcut hints', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeAll(() => {
    initGlobalShortcut();
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    document.body.replaceChildren();
  });

  test('AC1 pressing a hint key focuses its box and hides the hint', () => {
    const search = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    const findFile = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    expect(press(document.body, 's').defaultPrevented).toBe(true);
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(search.input);
    expect(search.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);

    search.input.blur();
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(findFile.input);
    expect(findFile.kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('AC2 Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away', () => {
    const {input, kbd} = renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    input.focus();
    input.value = 'needle';
    press(input, 'Escape');
    expect(input.value).toBe('');
    expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(input);
    expect(kbd.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('AC8 a hint that loads again keeps its key working', () => {
    const before = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    before.wrapper.remove(); // as moving through the file tree replaces the page content
    const after = renderHint('t', 'Go to file');
    press(document.body, 't');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(after.input);
  });

  test('AC8 a second hint for the same key on the page throws', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…');
    expect(() => renderHint('s', 'Search issues…')).toThrow('conflicts with "s"');
  });

  test('AC9 a hint is listed with its box\'s placeholder and its section', () => {
    renderHint('s', 'Search code…', 'Repository');
    renderHint('t', 'Go to file', 'Repository');
    renderHint('x', 'No section');
    expect(getShortcuts()).toEqual([
      {keys: 's', description: 'Search code…', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 't', description: 'Go to file', section: 'Repository'},
      {keys: 'x', description: 'No section', section: undefined},
    ]);
  });
});

export function randomString(length: number): string {

function apiAuthHeader(username: string, password: string) {
  return {Authorization: `Basic ${globalThis.btoa(`${username}:${password}`)}`};
}

export function apiHeaders() {
  return apiAuthHeader(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD);
}

async function apiRetry(fn: () => Promise<{ok: () => boolean; status: () => number; text: () => Promise<string>}>, label: string) {
  const maxAttempts = 5;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const response = await fn();
    if (response.ok()) return;
    if ([500, 502, 503].includes(response.status()) && attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 500;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * (attempt + 1) + jitter));
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${response.status()} ${await response.text()}`);
  }
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER_RUNTIME="${CONTAINER_RUNTIME:-docker}"
CONTAINER_NAME="gitea-e2e-runner-$$"

free_port() {
  node -e "const s=require('net').createServer();s.listen(0,'127.0.0.1',()=>{process.stdout.write(String(s.address().port));s.close()})"
}

detect_playwright_mode() {
  if [ "${PLAYWRIGHT_MODE:-auto}" = "local" ] || [ "${PLAYWRIGHT_MODE:-auto}" = "container" ]; then
    return
  fi

  PLAYWRIGHT_MODE="local"

  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Linux" ]; then
    # playwright only supports ubuntu/debian officially
    if ! grep -qE '^ID(_LIKE)?=.*(ubuntu|debian)' /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null; then
        PLAYWRIGHT_MODE="container"
    fi
  fi
}

wait_for_container() {
  local max_wait=30
  local elapsed=0
  echo "Waiting for container to start..."
  while ! (echo > "/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PLAYWRIGHT_SERVER_PORT") 2>/dev/null; do
    if [ "$("$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$CONTAINER_NAME" 2>/dev/null)" != "true" ]; then
      echo "Error: container exited before becoming ready." >&2
      "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" logs "$CONTAINER_NAME" >&2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    if [ "$elapsed" -ge "$max_wait" ]; then
      echo "Error: container did not become ready after ${max_wait}s." >&2
      "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" logs "$CONTAINER_NAME" >&2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    sleep 1
    elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
  done
  echo "Container is ready."
}

CMD="${1:-run}"
if [ "$CMD" = "install" ] || [ "$CMD" = "run" ]; then
  [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
else
  CMD="run"
fi

detect_playwright_mode

if [ "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODE" = "container" ]; then
  if ! command -v "$CONTAINER_RUNTIME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "error: PLAYWRIGHT_MODE=container but '$CONTAINER_RUNTIME' is not installed." >&2
    echo "Install docker/podman or set CONTAINER_RUNTIME to an available runtime." >&2
    exit 1

export async function login(page: Page, username = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, password = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD) {
  const response = await page.request.post('/user/login', {

  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
}

/* asserts the child has no horizontal inset from its parent — catches padding/border anywhere
 * in between regardless of which element declares it */
export async function assertFlushWithParent(child: Locator, parent: Locator) {
  const [childBox, parentBox] = await Promise.all([child.boundingBox(), parent.boundingBox()]);
  if (!childBox || !parentBox) throw new Error('boundingBox returned null');
  expect(childBox.x).toBe(parentBox.x);
  expect(childBox.width).toBe(parentBox.width);
}

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, assertNoJsError, randomString} from './utils.ts';

async function createRepo(page: Page) {
  const repoName = `e2e-shortcut-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, repoName, 'other.txt', 'other file');
  return `/${env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER}/${repoName}`;
}

test('s and t focus their boxes, and Escape clears them', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  const searchHint = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd');
  const goToFile = page.getByRole('combobox');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the Vue box has mounted and registered
  await expect(searchHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');

  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.type('st');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('st');
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('');
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeVisible();

  await page.keyboard.press('t');
  await expect(goToFile).toBeFocused();
  await expect(goToFileHint).toBeHidden();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('t keeps working after moving through the file tree', async ({page}) => {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  await page.goto(`${repoLink}/src/branch/main/README.md`);
  await page.locator('.repo-view-file-tree-toggle[data-toggle-action="show"]').click();
  const goToFile = page.getByRole('combobox');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');

  for (const [file, content] of [['other.txt', 'other file'], ['README.md', 'e2e-shortcut-']]) {
    await page.locator(`#view-file-tree .tree-item[title="${file}"]`).click();
    await expect(page.locator('.file-view')).toContainText(content); // the page content was swapped
    await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the new hint has registered
    await page.keyboard.press('t');
    await expect(goToFile).toBeFocused();
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  }
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

Commit 5 is ready for you to review: a new file, `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts`. Both tests pass locally against your `make watch`, in about 1.1 s each.

**What it tests**
- **Repo home (AC1, AC2, AC9):** both hints carry the Repository section. `s` focuses the search box and hides its hint, typing `st` just types, and Escape clears the box, moves focus away and brings the hint back. `t` then focuses "Go to file".
- **File view (AC8):** it moves to `other.txt` and back through the file tree. After each move it waits for the content to swap and the new hint to register, then checks `t` focuses the new box.
- Both tests end with `assertNoJsError`.

**Checks**
- Break-it check: removing the line that lets a reloaded hint replace its stale entry fails the file-tree test. The file is restored, and the run on the restored code passes.
- `make lint-js` and `git diff --check` are clean.

That button is hidden because the tree is shown by default for anonymous users and new accounts (`routers/web/repo/view_home.go` → `prepareHomeTreeSideBarSwitch`), so I removed the click. # AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
########## PR 67
feat(issues): backend implementation of close issue reason 
Closes #53

## What changed and why

Gitea records *that* an issue or pull request was closed, but not *why*. This PR adds the backend for a close reason: completed, not planned, duplicate of another issue, or other (with a short description). #54 (UI) and #55 (API) build on it.

- Issues and pull requests can store a close reason. Existing ones start with none.
- The timeline entry for each close keeps its own copy of the reason. Reopening clears the issue's current reason, but the history keeps what each close said.
- An invalid reason is refused and the issue stays open:
  - A pull request can't be closed as completed.
  - "Other" needs a description of up to 255 characters.
  - A duplicate must point to another issue in the same repository.
- Every existing way of closing works as before and records no reason.
- The router for the close form on the issue page can now error messages related to invalid close reason, following existing functionality. The front end work, thus, does not need to modify this.
- Docs in `.claude-students` are updated.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** after the migration, every existing issue, pull request and close entry reads as having no reason.
- **AC2:** closing with any of the four reasons stores it on the issue and in its close entry.
- **AC3:** a description that is empty, only spaces, or longer than 255 characters is refused, and the issue stays open. A valid description is stored exactly as typed.
- **AC4:** a duplicate that doesn't exist, is the issue itself, or is in another repository is refused. A valid one is stored, and its number, title and link can be shown.
- **AC5:** a pull request can't be closed as completed; issues can use all four reasons.
- **AC6:** reopening clears the issue's reason; the earlier close entry keeps its own.
- **AC7:** existing close paths are unchanged, and a merge records no reason.

## How it was tested

Mostly unit tests against the test database, plus one integration test that submits the real close form. To confirm the tests would catch mistakes, key lines were deliberately broken one at a time, and each break made a test fail.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | The migration on existing open and closed issues and PRs; a fresh install; old close entries |
| AC2 | Closing with each reason, directly and through the web form |
| AC3 | Empty, spaces-only and too-long descriptions are refused and the issue stays open; valid text is kept as typed |
| AC4 | Self, missing and other-repository duplicates are refused; a valid one is stored and loaded; a deleted target doesn't break the page |
| AC5 | The allowed reasons for issues and PRs; a PR closed as completed is refused |
| AC6 | Reopening after "other" and after "duplicate" |
| AC7 | Merging records no reason; the existing tests for the close button, the API, merging, commit keywords and branch deletion still pass |

The tests are in `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`, `models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go`, `services/forms/repo_form_test.go`, `services/pull/merge_test.go` and `tests/integration/issue_test.go`.


**Verification run:** 
An automated run passed every build, lint and test check, and a code review covered correctness, regressions, databases, security, conventions, tests and docs. It found no defects against the acceptance criteria. The minor issues it found were fixed (comment wording, one misleading error message, two missing test cases, and doc inaccuracies). These were reviewed by me to ensure that the changes actually made sense, instead of false positives.

**Change to mock data**
Since three more columns were added to the issues table, the CI were failing due to the expectation of a different _size._ of data Thus, the file names were adjusted to expect the new amount of data, specifically a batch size limit of 41. Upon changing this, all four of the previously failing tests (representing the four DBs) passed.

## Known limitations

- Closing with a comment and a refused reason still posts the comment. This matches how the existing "blocked by dependencies" refusal behaves. A description that is too long is the exception: the form refuses the whole request, so nothing is posted.
- If the issue a duplicate points to is deleted later, the closed issue still refers to it, and the page treats it as not found.
- For #54: the duplicate target is loaded without checking whether the viewer may see it. It is always in the same repository, but #54 should check the viewer can read issues or pull requests before showing it.
- For #54 and #55: the reason names are only mapped on the web form. The API will need the same mapping.
- The 255-character limit uses Gitea's standard form length rule (`MaxSize`), which counts characters. MSSQL counts an emoji as two, so on MSSQL only, a description of more than about 127 emoji passes that rule but is too long for the column.


## AI assistance

Claude code draft the code, tests, docs and other changes. I made the decisions, refused to let claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I can review them.

PR written through back and forth between human and AI.
########## PR 68
feat(issues): frontend implementation of close issue reason 
Closes #54

## What changed and why

#53 stores and checks why an issue or pull request was closed, but nothing on the page let you choose a reason or see one. This PR adds the UI for it.

- **Close button:** on an issue or pull request page it becomes a split button that names its reason. The ▾ lists the reasons that item may use, and the button text follows the pick, with or without a comment typed. This was done for both showing the default reason that would be submitted, but also to reflect the chosen option.
- **Duplicate and Other:** each asks for its detail in a small popup under the button, reusing, for the most part, components that already existed in Gitea. A close without a usable value isn't sent; the popup reopens with the box marked red instead.
- **Timeline:** the close event says why: "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate" with a link with the number below it, or the Other text, shown as plain text.
- **Icons and labels:** closed items show their reason in lists, in the label at the top of the page and on the timeline badge. The color scheme follows what the current Gitea follows to keep things consistent. Items closed without a reason look as they do today.
- **Bulk close:** the list's Close button works the same way. The Issues tab offers Completed and Not planned, and the Pull Requests tab only Not planned (only a single option, but maintained the split for consistency).
- **Two of #53's known limitations are resolved:** a duplicate's title and link are only shown to viewers who can read the original, and the reason names now live in the model rather than the form, so #55's API can reuse them.
- The old, now unused button strings are removed, and the docs in `.claude-students` are updated.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** the button starts on Completed for an issue and Not planned for a pull request, so a plain click closes with that reason.
- **AC2:** the menu offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other on an issue, and the same without Completed on a pull request. Merging is unchanged.
- **AC3:** picking another reason updates the button text, with or without a comment, and the last pick is the one saved.
- **AC4:** a number that isn't an issue or pull request in the repository, or is the item itself, is marked red with a message and the close isn't sent; the server refuses it too (#53). A valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- **AC5:** an empty description blocks the close, and the box stops at 255 characters; the server refuses both too (#53). The text is saved and shown as plain text.
- **AC6:** bulk Close offers Completed and Not planned on the Issues tab and only Not planned on the Pull Requests tab, and every selected item closes with the picked reason.
- **AC7:** the close event states the reason.
- **AC8:** each reason has its own icon and label; items with no reason look as before.
- **AC9:** reopening brings back the open look, and the earlier close event keeps its reason.
- **AC10:** every new string is in `locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file changed.


## How it was tested

Testing was done in three distinct parts. 
- Vitest tests and integration tests to prove the functioning of the UI in the code itself. The tests themselves were tested by deliberately breaking code to see the changes and tests fail.
- A visual inspection of the changes by running a local instance. Since the changes were performed in small sets, the checks ensured only the behavior of the targeted portions changed, and nothing else.
- Claude running a headless browser with its own credentials to test the program and fix issues as it spotted them.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Each page's button starts on its default, and a plain close saves it |
| AC2 | The menu's reasons and labels on an issue and a pull request; a closed item only offers Reopen |
| AC3 | Picking changes the button text and the reason sent, with and without a comment typed |
| AC4 | The preview of the typed number; a missing number, the item itself, text or a non-whole number blocks the close; the timeline link |
| AC5 | Other's text is sent as typed; empty or spaces-only blocks the close; the 255 limit; HTML and Markdown in the timeline stay plain text |
| AC6 | Both tabs' menus; bulk closing several issues with each reason and a pull request as not planned; a refused reason leaves the item open |
| AC7 | The timeline text for each reason, and for a close with no reason |
| AC8 | The list icon, page label and timeline badge for each reason and for none; a merged pull request still looks merged |
| AC9 | Reopening shows the open look again, and the earlier close keeps its reason |
| AC10 | Labels are checked as rendered text, so a missing key would show up as the key itself |

The tests are in `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`, `tests/integration/issue_test.go`, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.test.ts`, `repo-issue-list.test.ts` and `repo-common.test.ts`. The Playwright test `tests/e2e/issue-comment.test.ts` now clicks the renamed button.


## Known limitations

- The hover popup on issue links still shows the old icon. It reads the API, so it is out of scope. The same problem occurs with duplicate preview.
- Bulk close shows no message when the server refuses a close, whether for a blocked dependency or a reason only a hand-made request can send. A "FIXME" was present for the relevant code, but was not changed since that would be way out of scope, impacting behavior that should not belong to this set of changes.
- Closing with a comment still posts the comment if the server then refuses the close. This should be highly unlikely, but since it is a general pattern to have the server be the final verifier of rules, blocking such behavior would not follow convention.
- A pull request closed as not planned has the same icon as an issue closed as not planned; its link still says which it is (Decision 8).
- The red message in the duplicate popup isn't announced by screen readers. Gitea doesn't use `aria-invalid` anywhere, so this follows it. However, the message _is_ read when the box gets focus.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I can review them with tests.

```markdown
Title: refactor(shortcut): central keyboard-shortcut registry with key sequences

Closes #56

## What changed and why

Gitea's keyboard shortcuts were one page-wide key handler that searched the page for a `<kbd>` hint showing the pressed key and focused the box beside it. That only allowed "press a letter to focus a box": no two-key sequences, no shortcut without a box, and nothing could list the shortcuts for a help dialog. This PR replaces it with one place to add shortcuts. Nothing changes for the user: `s` and `t` work as before. #57 (help dialog), #58 (`g` shortcuts), #59 (`c` shortcuts) and #60 (turning shortcuts off) build on it.

- **One call to add a shortcut:** `registerShortcut()` takes the keys, a translated description, an optional section and the action to run. `getShortcuts()` lists the shortcuts on the current page, for the help dialog in #57.
- **Two-key sequences** such as `g c`: the second key must come within 1500 ms. Pressing `g` does nothing else while it waits, and a key that doesn't finish a sequence counts as a fresh press.
- **Shortcuts stay out of the way:** nothing runs while typing in a field, while Ctrl, Alt or Cmd is held, or when a widget such as a menu has already used the key.
- **Clashes fail loudly:** adding the same keys twice, or keys where one starts the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), throws an error instead of one silently winning.
- **A shortcut can belong to part of the page,** and only exists while that part is on the page. This is what lets the `T` hint come back after moving through the file tree, which swaps the page content, without counting as a clash.
- **The `S` and `T` hints register themselves** through the new code. Each is listed with its box's placeholder ("Search code…", "Go to file") and the existing "Repository" string as its section, so no new string was needed.
- The docs in `.claude-students` are updated: a recipe for adding a shortcut, and a correction to how translated `data-` attributes are named.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box and hides its hint; `t` does the same for "Go to file" on file and folder views.
- **AC2:** Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away, as before.
- **AC3:** a single-key shortcut such as `?` runs once, and the key does nothing else.
- **AC4:** `g` then `c` within 1500 ms runs the sequence once, and neither key runs a shortcut of its own.
- **AC5:** after more than 1500 ms, or after a key that doesn't finish any sequence, the `g` is dropped and the next key is a fresh press.
- **AC6:** keys typed into an input, textarea, select or editable area run no shortcut and type as normal.
- **AC7:** a key a widget has already used runs no shortcut and drops a half-typed sequence.
- **AC8:** adding the same keys again, or keys where one starts the other, throws; a hint that loads again after file-tree navigation is not an error, and its key keeps working.
- **AC9:** each listed shortcut has its keys, description and, if given, section; `s` and `t` use their box's placeholder and are in the Repository section.

## How it was tested

Testing was done in three parts:
- **Unit tests (Vitest)** for the registry and the hints, 17 in total. To confirm they would catch mistakes, key lines were deliberately broken one at a time (the menu check, the fresh-press retry, the timeout boundary, the hint's action, the Escape clear, the section), and each break made the matching test fail.
- **Playwright tests** that drive the real pages, since the unit tests can't render Gitea's templates or mount the Vue "Go to file" box. Breaking the code that lets a reloaded hint replace the old one made the file-tree test fail.
- **A headless-browser walkthrough** by Claude on a local instance, which also checked `/devtest/keyboard-shortcut`, that typing in the box doesn't trigger shortcuts, that Ctrl+S is ignored, and that the page shows no JavaScript errors.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Pressing `s` and `t` focuses each box and hides its hint, in the unit tests and on a real repository page |
| AC2 | Escape clears the box, moves focus away and brings the hint back |
| AC3 | A single key runs its action once and is used up; an unregistered key is left alone; case doesn't matter and Shift alone isn't a press |
| AC4 | `g c` within 1500 ms runs once, and a single-key `c` doesn't run |
| AC5 | Waiting past 1500 ms, or pressing a key that finishes no sequence, drops the `g` and treats the key as a fresh press |
| AC6 | Input, textarea, select and editable areas run nothing; typing into a field drops a half-typed sequence; on a real page, typing `st` in the search box just types |
| AC7 | A key a widget already used runs nothing and drops a half-typed sequence; Ctrl, Alt and Cmd presses run nothing |
| AC8 | Duplicate and overlapping keys throw; a shortcut whose element left the page gives way to a new one; on a real page, `t` still works after moving through the file tree twice |
| AC9 | The list gives keys, description and section, and drops a shortcut whose element left the page; a hint is listed with its box's placeholder and section; the real hints carry the Repository section |

The tests are in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts`. AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC7 are covered by unit tests only, because no page has a sequence, a `?` shortcut or a type-ahead menu next to a hint until #57–#59 add them.

## CI / manual verification

- `make test-frontend`: 354 tests in 60 files pass, including the 17 new ones.
- `make lint-js` (eslint and vue-tsc), `make lint-templates` and `make lint-editorconfig` pass.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` passes for every doc this PR touches; it still reports `models-issues.md` being over its line cap, which is already the case on `main`.
- The Playwright tests pass locally on Chromium, Playwright's Firefox and the system Firefox, and on a Firefox with fingerprinting protection turned on. `make test-e2e` needs docker on this machine, so they were run against a local instance instead; the PR's e2e job runs them on all three browsers.
- An automated review of correctness against the ACs, conventions, course rules, docs and tests found no defects.

## Design

See Design Decisions 1 (shortcuts kept in one list, each optionally tied to part of the page) and 2 (each hint names its own section) on #56.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** A shortcut tied to an element counts as present while the element is on the page, even when it is hidden. That is enough for the `S` and `T` hints, but #58 and #59, whose shortcuts should only work while their tab or button is shown, will have to tie them to something that is removed or check visibility themselves.

**Encountered:**
- Moving through the file tree swaps the page content but never unmounts the Vue "Go to file" box inside it, so each move leaves one detached copy behind. Handled by not relying on cleanup: a shortcut tied to an element that has left the page is replaced when its hint registers again. Not fixed here.
- Gitea's page setup (`data-global-init`) has no error isolation: if one element's setup throws while the page loads, every element after it is left unset. A second hint for the same key now throws there (AC8), so that mistake would break the rest of the page's setup. This follows the existing pattern, as setup already throws on other developer mistakes such as a misspelled function name. Not fixed here.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, ran the headless-browser checks and an automated review. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on #56.

    // only restore when focus is still in the popup, so focus moved elsewhere by an item handler is kept
    const focusInPopup = this.popup.contains(document.activeElement);
    hideElem(this.popup);
    this.trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDownOutside, {capture: true});
    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
  }

  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
  };

  // a native button fires "click" on Space keyup, which would toggle the menu shut again or double-activate an item
  preventSpaceClick = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault();
  };

  onTriggerKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      this.open('first');
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      this.open('last');
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  onPopupKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    const items = this.items();
    const current = items.indexOf(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (e.key === 'Tab') {
      // focus the trigger and let the default action move on from there
      this.close(true);
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      e.stopPropagation(); // don't also close a surrounding modal
      this.close(true);
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      items[(current + 1) % items.length].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      items.at(current <= 0 ? -1 : current - 1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Home') {
      items[0].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'End') {
      items.at(-1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      if (current < 0) return;
      items[current].click();
    } else if (e.key.length === 1 && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      this.focusByFirstChar(items, current, e.key);
    } else {
      return;
    }

629857470c test(shortcut): check a key the language menu used runs no shortcut (#56)
2c83c3b46c test(shortcut): add e2e tests for the S and T hints (#56)
Title: refactor(shortcut): central keyboard-shortcut registry with key sequences

Closes #56

## What changed and why

Gitea's keyboard shortcuts were one page-wide key handler that searched the page for a `<kbd>` hint showing the pressed key and focused the box beside it. That only allowed "press a letter to focus a box": no two-key sequences, no shortcut without a box, and nothing could list the shortcuts for a help dialog. This PR replaces it with one place to add shortcuts. Nothing changes for the user and `s` and `t` work as before.

- **One call to add a shortcut:** `registerShortcut()` takes the keys, a translated description, an optional section and the action to run. `getShortcuts()` lists the shortcuts on the current page, for the help dialog in #57.
- **Two-key sequences** such as `g c`: the second key must come within 1500 ms. Pressing `g` does nothing else while it waits, and a key that doesn't finish a sequence counts as a fresh press.
- **Shortcuts stay out of the way:** nothing runs while typing in a field, while Ctrl, Alt or Cmd is held, or when a widget such as a menu has already used the key.
- **Clashes fail loudly:** adding the same keys twice, or keys where one starts the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), throws an error instead of one silently winning.
- **A shortcut can belong to part of the page,** and only exists while that part is on the page. This is what lets the `T` hint come back after moving through the file tree, which swaps the page content, without counting as a clash.
- **The `S` and `T` hints register themselves** through the new code. Each is listed with its box's placeholder ("Search code…", "Go to file") and the existing "Repository" string as its section, so no new string was needed.
- The docs in `.claude-students` are updated with additions and corrections from this implementation

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box and hides its hint; `t` does the same for "Go to file" on file and folder views.
- **AC2:** Escape in a box with a hint clears it and moves focus away, as before.
- **AC3:** a single-key shortcut such as `?` runs once, and the key does nothing else.
- **AC4:** `g` then `c` within 1500 ms runs the sequence once, and neither key runs a shortcut of its own.
- **AC5:** after more than 1500 ms, or after a key that doesn't finish any sequence, the `g` is dropped and the next key is a fresh press.
- **AC6:** keys typed into an input, textarea, select or editable area run no shortcut and type as normal.
- **AC7:** a key a widget has already used runs no shortcut and drops a half-typed sequence.
- **AC8:** adding the same keys again, or keys where one starts the other, throws; a hint that loads again after file-tree navigation is not an error, and its key keeps working.
- **AC9:** each listed shortcut has its keys, description and, if given, section; `s` and `t` use their box's placeholder and are in the Repository section.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

There were no tests for keyboard shortcuts before this PR, so every test here is new.

- **Unit tests (Vitest) for the logic.** Most of the changes related to rules about which key presses run which shortcut. These need no server, so they are tested on their own with a fake clock so the timeout tests don't have to wait. The registry tests each build their own list of shortcuts, and the hint tests clear the page after each test, so no test leaks into another. 17 tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.
- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** The `S` and `T` hints only work once Gitea's templates, the Vue "Go to file" box and the page setup code have all run, and none of that exists in a unit test. Three tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` drive real pages to test all the changes and rules implemented.

**Testing the tests.** Mutation testing performed during implementation of tests to ensure they actually catch the intended errors. Each break made the matching test fail, so the tests check the behaviour and don't just run.

**Not covered automatically, and why.** AC3, AC4 and AC5 have no real-page test, because no page has a sequence or a `?` shortcut yet; they get one when #57 and #58 add them.

**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance, and I had a look to ensure the changes actually did not change visible/user facing behavior.

**Misc.** Token heavy review workflow with reviewers and critics was run at the end to ensure things were not overlooked.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Pressing `s` and `t` focuses each box and hides its hint, in the unit tests and on a real repository page |
| AC2 | Escape clears the box, moves focus away and brings the hint back, in both |
| AC3 | A single key runs its action once and is used up; an unregistered key is left alone; case doesn't matter and Shift alone isn't a press |
| AC4 | `g c` within 1500 ms runs once, and a single-key `c` doesn't run |
| AC5 | Waiting past 1500 ms, or pressing a key that finishes no sequence, drops the `g` and treats the key as a fresh press |
| AC6 | Input, textarea, select and editable areas run nothing; typing into a field drops a half-typed sequence; on a real page, typing `st` in the search box just types |
| AC7 | A key a widget already used runs nothing and drops a half-typed sequence; Ctrl, Alt and Cmd presses run nothing; on a real page, `s` in the language menu jumps to a language and the search box stays unfocused |
| AC8 | Duplicate and overlapping keys throw; a shortcut whose element left the page gives way to a new one; on a real page, `t` still works after moving through the file tree twice |
| AC9 | The list gives keys, description and section, and drops a shortcut whose element left the page; a hint is listed with its box's placeholder and section; the real hints carry the Repository section |

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #56.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** A shortcut tied to an element counts as present while the element is on the page, even when it is hidden. That is enough for the `S` and `T` hints, but #58 and #59, whose shortcuts should only work while their tab or button is shown, will have to tie them to something that is removed or check visibility themselves. In other words, any shortcuts need to "attach" themselves to an element with the same lifetime as themselves to avoid clashes.

**Encountered:**
- Moving through the file tree swaps the page content but never unmounts the Vue "Go to file" box inside it, so each move leaves one detached copy behind. Handled by not relying on cleanup: a shortcut tied to an element that has left the page is replaced when its hint registers again. Not fixed here.
- Gitea's page setup (`data-global-init`) has no error isolation: if one element's setup throws while the page loads, every element after it is left unset. A second hint for the same key now throws there (AC8), so that mistake would break the rest of the page's setup. This follows the existing pattern, as setup already throws on other developer mistakes such as a misspelled function name. Not fixed here.
